display.purpose: H1 hero headline only, one per page.

label.purpose: Uppercase section-opener kicker, paired with the short dash.

motion.name: ease-out-signature
motion.purpose: Gallery photo slow-zoom on hover and scroll-reveal transitions (0.7-1.2s).

motion.name: wave-drift
motion.purpose: Barely-perceptible continuous horizontal drift of the signal-wave SVG divider; suggested default pending final tuning. Disabled entirely under prefers-reduced-motion.

narrative.overview:
This is the term the client's own 2024 brochure already earned, and it's the standard the site is held to: the site should read like the print collateral of a serious electrical-engineering contractor — deep navy, generous white space, confident large-scale type, one restrained signature graphic — not like a SaaS product landing page. Every decision below defaults to restraint. The system rejects gradients, glassmorphism, decorative card shadows, and the stock-photography-and-superlative vocabulary of the prior WordPress site.

Density is generous but purposeful: sections carry one idea each (per PRODUCT.md's Design Principles), separated by real vertical space rather than dividers or shadows. The one permitted piece of ornament is the signal-wave motif — a thin electrical-waveform line, lifted directly from the brochure, used as a section divider with a barely-perceptible horizontal drift. Everything else earns its place through structure (borders, type scale, color role) rather than decoration.
keyCharacteristics: Deep navy + paper-white base, with leaf-green and signal-blue reserved for small, deliberate accents only
Large, confident, geometric-expanded display type paired with a neutral, highly readable body face
Flat surfaces throughout — depth comes from borders and translucent dark overlay panels, never box-shadow
One recurring signature element (the signal wave), not a library of decorative motifs
Mobile-first, touch-parity by construction: nothing shown only on hover

rules.name: The Leaf Rarity Rule
rules.body: leaf-500 never fills a background, a button, or a section. It appears only as a small accent — an icon, a chip, a bullet — and its rarity is what keeps it feeling like the logo's signature color rather than a UI color.

rules.name: The Navy Ramp Rule
rules.body: navy-950 → navy-900 → navy-700 → navy-100 is a single continuous tonal ramp, not four unrelated colors. Any new navy-family need should sit on this same ramp.

rules.name: The No-Fluff Rule
rules.body: Copy is short, factual, and technically specific (norms, equipment, kV ratings) rather than motivational. If a sentence could appear on any B2B site regardless of industry, cut it.

rules.name: The Deliberate Eyebrow Rule
rules.body: The eyebrow-dash-title pattern is inherited directly from the client's print brochure — it is brand continuity, not a default scaffold. Apply it as a single consistent system, and vary section rhythm through spacing, StatBar, marquee, and full-bleed gallery breaks so the eyebrow doesn't become the only structural device on the page.

rules.name: The Flat-by-Default Rule
rules.body: No box-shadow anywhere in the system, including the mobile nav panel, sticky header, and lightbox. Where a SaaS pattern would reach for a shadow, use a border, a background-color shift, or a navy-950 translucent panel instead.

dos: Do keep leaf-500 to micro-accents only — an icon, a chip, a bullet.
Do build all depth from 1px borders and navy-950 translucent panels, never box-shadow.
Do write explicit, task-specific button labels ("Chiamaci ora", "Scrivici via email"), never "Invia" / "Submit".
Do cap body copy at 65ch measure at every breakpoint.
Do keep the two radius scales distinct: 6px for buttons, 2px for cards/containers.
Do keep the tel: CTA visible in the header at every breakpoint, and in the mobile sticky bar below md.
Do show gallery captions, metadata, and chip tags by default — never hover-only.
Do disable the signal-wave drift, StatBar counters, and all scroll-reveal animation under prefers-reduced-motion.
donts: Don't use leaf-500 as a section or button background — it is a logo accent, not a UI color.
Don't add box-shadow to cards, the mobile nav panel, the sticky header, or the lightbox.
Don't use gradients, background-clip: text, or glassmorphism anywhere.
Don't use stock photography of "smiling guys in hardhats" — source real photography of the actual substations, vans, and control room.
Don't build the projects gallery as Pinterest-style masonry, a uniform square-thumbnail grid, an autoplay carousel, a 50%-black-overlay-with-centered-title, or a flip/tilt hover card.
Don't use pill-shaped buttons; radius is 6px, full stop.
Don't let the eyebrow-dash pattern become the only section-opening device on a page.
